values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/lakedubonnetforest ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Lake Dubonnet State Forest Campground, Grand Traverse: 50 sites, $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boat ramp access to Lake Dubonnet from the campground.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/lakedubonnetforest ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'There is boat ramp access to Lake Dubonnet from the campground.'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: First-come only, but registration is now by phone or online (using the number or website posted at the campground), no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. No advance payments or reservations.

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/lakedubonnetforest ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.' 'All registrations at this campground processed online or via phone' 'You can register no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of your arrival.' 'we do not accept advance payments or reservations') + amenity table (Lake Dubonnet State Forest Campground: 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 50 'tent and small trailer' sites (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/lakedubonnetforest ('Lake Dubonnet's rustic campground offers 50 tent and small trailer sites along the tranquil shores of Lake Dubonnet.'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (50 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground among soaring pines on Lake Dubonnet, 4.2 mi NW of Interlochen via US-31 South and Gonder Road (Grand Traverse County); managed by Interlochen State Park. The Lost Lake Pathway (hiking, ungroomed skiing, snowshoeing) runs through the campground; ORVs may be ridden from the campsite to local ORV routes. The separate Lake Dubonnet Trail Camp is not part of this entry. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 50 tent/small-trailer sites (confirmed), $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only (now registered by phone/online from 8 a.m. on arrival day), 15-day maximum (all confirmed, registration note new). Season (open all year, roads not plowed) already manual and matches. Boat ramp. Not equestrian (type 'rustic'). Note trimmed of field restatements.
